stage_a.note: Very strong positive expression, highly enthusiastic and powerful delivery.
Pronounced, sustained engagement and excitement throughout the pitch.
Very friendly, approachable, smiling, and positively oriented toward the investors.

venture.description: A designer lifestyle apparel brand combining fashion and comfort to inspire and empower youth.
venture.note: The founders are a mother and her teenage son.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey introduces himself and his millionaire mindset, stating the ask for the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell introduces the brand as a designer lifestyle apparel brand combining fashion and comfort.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey shares his story of starting the business at twelve with birthday money and retiring his mom.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond handles the products and remarks on them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin handles the products.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond expresses how much he likes the green sample.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark comments on the blue sample.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks about the origin of the brand name.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey explains the name combines sports and heroes, with go for go-getters.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark encourages Trey.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond praises the high quality and the use of embroidery over patches.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey thanks Daymond for the compliment.

turns.summary: Sherell states the cost to make the lion sweatsuit.

turns.summary: Sherell states the retail price for the sweatsuits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert remarks on the premium positioning.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell confirms it is a premium brand.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks them to elaborate on the story of selling out t-shirts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey recounts selling his first shirts at barbershops and reinvesting to grow the brand.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell adds that Trey would wake her up early to go sell.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark jokes about Trey waking his mom up.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell confirms Mark's joke.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell explains Trey's drive to continually increase his sales goals and reinvest all earnings.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark applauds Trey's work ethic.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what motivates customers to buy the products so enthusiastically.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey explains the brand represents a feeling and inspires youth to chase their dreams.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks about their social media following.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey states their large follower counts on Instagram.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what inspired Trey to start a clothing line.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey explains he wanted to be a positive role model in his challenging Philadelphia neighborhood.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell adds that clothing was essential in their household due to her background and church.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for the total sales figure to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey states their impressive total sales figure.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement at the sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for clarification on the time period for those sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey breaks down the sales year by year, showing massive growth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark claps in amazement at the numbers.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks to confirm their sales channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey confirms they currently have three physical locations.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert asks for the split between online and physical retail sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey provides the percentage breakdown between physical and online sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert expresses how blown away he is by Trey's maturity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks how they are driving so much traffic to their business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey recounts how a connection led to a social media post from Diddy, causing massive sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell adds that Diddy also provided a grant to help them open a physical store.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks for their projected total sales for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey provides the projected sales figure for the year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks about their year-to-date profit.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell states their profit figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks to verify if that profit is before or after paying themselves.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell clarifies the profit is after they have been paid.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin expresses amazement.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what they intend to do with the investment money.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell outlines plans to hire a designer and e-commerce help to sustain growth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond questions why they need an investor when they are already highly successful.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sherell explains they need capital to produce inventory further ahead of the current season.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey adds that they are in a position for massive growth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond challenges whether they truly need a partner given their current trajectory.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori decides she is not the best fit and exits the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey and Sherell thank Lori.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin states apparel is not his area of expertise and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey thanks Kevin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Robert expresses concern over the heavy reliance on brick-and-mortar retail and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey thanks Robert.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark offers exactly what they asked for but for a larger equity stake to help guide them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks Daymond if he wants to partner on the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond declines to partner, stating he does not need Mark for a clothing deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond matches Mark's offer independently.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey and Sherell react to having two competing offers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey counters Daymond, asking if he would accept a slightly lower equity stake.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond immediately accepts Trey's counter-offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trey and Sherell celebrate and accept the deal with Daymond.

decisions.note: Feels she is not the best partner for them.
Not a clothing guy, not his space.
Scared by the 70% brick and mortar sales.
Wants to help young superstars walk to the vision.
Matches Mark's offer, relates to starting a clothing brand with his mother.
Counters Daymond's offer asking for 20% equity.
Celebrates and accepts the revised offer.

record.notes: Sherell (F2) is Trey's (F1) mother. She steps in to answer detailed operational questions while Trey handles the brand story and vision.
